title: AGGREGATE: is the dual-order TIE rule protective or lossy, and can an order-symmetric tie-break recover the frontier order? (392 calls)
question: The 49 tied questions in each of the deployed-grok-reference and oracle-reference runs, with two order-symmetric tie-breaks: REPLICATE (two further calls, one per order, majority of four) and GRADE (pointwise grades, higher wins); (1) accuracy on the ties against 0.000 by convention; (2) overall accuracy; (3) arx win rate at p < 0.05; (4) residual ties.

plain_description.what: The judge sees each pair of answers twice, once in each order. When the two readings disagree it records a tie. This test took the 49 ties in two earlier runs and tried two ways to break them fairly: ask the judge twice more and take the majority, or have it grade each answer separately.
plain_description.why: It checks whether those ties hide real information the judge throws away, and whether resolving them would let the judge recover the true order of the strongest models.
plain_description.information: If the ties can be settled correctly, the judge becomes more accurate for only a few extra calls. If the strongest-model order still does not come out right, judge noise is not the only obstacle. Result: done. Asking twice more settles most ties correctly and raises overall accuracy by about 8 points for about 16% more calls. It does not recover the order of the strongest models: ordering two models 1.7 points apart is beyond this judge on this corpus. Later ruled history rather than evidence, because it ran on the older question pool.
